hero.description: Friday's global briefing examines US–Iran diplomacy, oil prices, Russia's war in Ukraine, European economic pressures, African currencies and Nigeria's refining industry.

breaking: US–Iran: President Donald Trump says Washington will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections, citing ongoing discussions.
Energy markets: Brent crude fell to around $103.53 a barrel in early Friday trading, according to Reuters, although prices remain volatile.
Ukraine: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticises Washington's approach following deadly Russian strikes and calls for stronger support.
Global markets: Asian shares remain under pressure as investors assess high energy prices, bond yields and the cost of artificial intelligence investment.
Nigeria: The Dangote Refinery's crude purchases and expanding role in fuel supply remain important developments for the country's energy sector.
Africa: Currency pressures persist in parts of the continent, while Nigeria's naira is expected to remain comparatively stable, according to Reuters reporting.

featured.title: US–Iran Talks Offer a Possible Diplomatic Opening as Oil Markets Remain Volatile
featured.content: President Donald Trump said the United States would not attack Iran before the American midterm elections on 3 November, pointing to what he described as productive discussions. Washington and Tehran remain divided over key issues, including nuclear enrichment and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices eased in early Friday trading, but the outlook remains uncertain as shipping risks, sanctions and diplomatic developments continue to influence energy markets.

articles.title: Trump Says US Will Not Attack Iran Before November Elections
articles.content: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Washington would not launch an attack on Iran before the 3 November midterm elections, citing ongoing discussions aimed at ending the conflict. The two sides have exchanged proposals, including issues connected to the Strait of Hormuz. However, major disagreements remain over Iran's nuclear programme and the terms of a possible settlement. Iran has rejected demands that it abandon uranium enrichment or surrender its uranium stockpile. No comprehensive peace agreement has been confirmed.
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump White House press conference

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains Central to Global Energy Security
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains a major concern for energy markets because it carries a substantial share of international oil and fuel shipments. Any prolonged disruption can affect shipping costs, supply availability and inflation in importing countries. Iran and the United States continue to discuss possible ways to end their conflict and restore normal maritime flows, but uncertainty remains over the timing and conditions for reopening the route.
articles.imageQuery: oil tanker ships Strait of Hormuz maritime shipping

articles.title: France Faces Renewed Pressure Over Schools and Public Protests
articles.content: French students took part in demonstrations and school blockades on Thursday as protests over school conditions continued in several cities. Some demonstrations were accompanied by violence. According to figures reported by France's Interior Ministry, approximately 71,500 people participated nationwide, including around 24,500 at the main Paris demonstration. The protests add to wider debate over education, public services and the challenges facing young people in France.

articles.title: European Markets Monitor Energy Costs and Financial Risks
articles.content: European investors continue to assess the consequences of geopolitical tensions, higher energy costs and changes in global borrowing conditions. Elevated oil prices can affect transport, manufacturing, household budgets and inflation. Financial markets are also watching government bond yields and the outlook for interest rates. The impact will vary across countries depending on their energy mix, public finances and exposure to international supply disruptions.
articles.imageQuery: European financial district stock market trading screens

articles.title: Ukraine Calls for Stronger Support Following Deadly Russian Strikes
articles.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticised the United States over its approach to the war after a series of deadly Russian attacks. Reuters reported that strikes over two days killed at least 78 people and injured 215, with a particularly deadly attack in Kramatorsk. Ukrainian officials have called for stronger air-defence assistance and additional pressure on Moscow. Casualty figures and responsibility for individual incidents should be read in the context of reporting from the authorities and news organisations covering the conflict.
articles.imageQuery: damaged buildings Ukraine emergency responders after airstrike

articles.title: US Policy on Iran Shapes Debate Ahead of Midterm Elections
articles.content: The Iran conflict has become an important domestic issue in the United States as voters face higher fuel costs and broader concerns about living expenses. Trump says discussions with Tehran are productive and has ruled out an attack before the November elections. However, a diplomatic breakthrough remains uncertain. The administration's handling of the conflict, its effect on energy prices and the future of US involvement are likely to remain subjects of political debate.
articles.imageQuery: United States Capitol building Washington DC

articles.title: Oil Prices Ease in Early Friday Trading After Trump's Comments
articles.content: Brent crude futures fell to approximately $103.53 a barrel and US West Texas Intermediate crude to around $90.97 in early Friday trading, according to Reuters. Prices eased after Trump said the United States would not attack Iran before the November elections and referred to ongoing discussions. Brent nevertheless remained on course for a weekly gain following earlier attacks on crude shipments from the Middle East. A hurricane threat to the US Gulf of Mexico region has also raised concerns about production disruptions. These prices reflect a specific trading snapshot and may change during the session.

articles.title: Global Shares Face Pressure From Bond Yields and AI Spending Concerns
articles.content: Global markets remain cautious as investors weigh energy prices, elevated bond yields and the enormous cost of developing artificial intelligence infrastructure. Reuters reported that Asian stocks were under pressure for a second consecutive week, while technology shares faced scrutiny over spending requirements and expected returns. Higher borrowing costs can affect businesses seeking finance, governments servicing debt and households using credit. Investors are increasingly assessing whether projected technology growth can justify the capital being committed.
articles.imageQuery: global stock market trading screens technology stocks

articles.title: African Currencies Face Uneven Pressures as Demand for Dollars Continues
articles.content: Foreign-exchange conditions remain mixed across Africa. Reuters reporting indicates that Uganda's shilling and Ghana's cedi are under pressure from demand for dollars linked to imports, energy and business activity. Nigeria's naira, by contrast, is expected to remain comparatively stable with support from central-bank dollar sales. Currency movements can influence the cost of imported goods, fuel, manufacturing inputs and external debt payments. Forecasts remain uncertain and should not be treated as guaranteed outcomes.
articles.imageQuery: African financial district business banking currency exchange

articles.title: Nigeria's Refining Industry Gains Importance Amid Global Supply Disruptions
articles.content: Nigeria's domestic refining capacity remains significant as international fuel markets face supply uncertainty. The Dangote Refinery has continued purchasing large volumes of Nigerian crude while preparing for a proposed public share offering. Reuters reported that the refinery had secured at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October arrival, equivalent to roughly 520,000 barrels per day. The final volume could change as additional purchases are made. Increased domestic processing may support fuel availability and exports, but prices and supply still depend on crude costs, logistics, refinery operations and market conditions.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote oil refinery Lekki Nigeria industrial facility

articles.title: Dangote Refinery's Crude Purchases Put Feedstock Supply in Focus
articles.content: The Dangote Refinery's planned public offering has drawn attention to the supply of crude oil needed to operate the facility. Reuters reported that purchases for October included Nigerian crude allocations and additional volumes acquired through tenders. The refinery's buying activity is relevant to Nigeria's crude-export market because greater domestic processing can reduce the amount available for export. Investors assessing the proposed listing should examine the company's operations, crude access, costs, competition and financial disclosures. Public interest in a share offering does not guarantee profits, and investments can lose value.
articles.imageQuery: oil refinery processing units Nigeria petroleum industry

articles.title: AI Investment Boom Faces Greater Scrutiny From Global Markets
articles.content: Artificial intelligence continues to attract substantial investment, but financial markets are paying closer attention to the cost of building data centres, securing computing capacity and developing advanced chips. Higher interest rates and borrowing costs can make large infrastructure projects more expensive. Investors are also examining whether companies can turn their spending into sustainable revenue. The debate is increasingly important to technology firms, suppliers, financial institutions and governments developing strategies for AI competitiveness.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence data centre server racks

articles.title: Middle East Tensions Continue to Affect Shipping and Consumer Costs
articles.content: Uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz has implications beyond crude oil. Shipping insurance, freight charges, refined fuels and other commodities can all be affected when important maritime routes face disruption. Higher transport and energy costs may eventually feed into food prices and the cost of manufactured goods. The scale of the impact will depend on how long disruptions last, whether alternative routes can handle additional volumes and whether diplomatic efforts produce a lasting agreement.
articles.imageQuery: commercial cargo ship containers international maritime trade

articles.title: Asian Economies Navigate Energy Risks and Technology Market Volatility
articles.content: Asian markets are contending with uncertainty over energy supplies, borrowing costs and technology-sector investment. Countries that import substantial quantities of oil can face higher production and transport expenses when crude prices rise. At the same time, companies involved in artificial intelligence and advanced technology continue to attract investment, although investors are increasingly examining valuations and spending plans. The region's economic outlook will depend on global demand, currency movements, energy prices and domestic policy decisions.

bigQuestion: As geopolitical tensions, energy prices and technological change increasingly affect everyday life, how can governments protect their citizens while maintaining economic stability and international cooperation?
